title: The plan was always going to slip
text: Students {{1}} asked to estimate {{2}} own thesis schedules, and then researchers simply waited. On average the projects took {{3}} longer than predicted, a finding so reliable it acquired a name: {{4}} is called the planning fallacy. {{5}}, telling people the base rates rarely helps; we listen, nod, and quietly believe our case is different. We plan {{6}} the best case because the best case is the story we can actually imagine, {{7}} the traffic, the illness and the lost password belong to other people's futures. The practical fix is unglamorous: ask {{8}} actually happened last time, write that number down, and start from there rather than from the dream.

gaps.explanation: Past passive with a plural subject: were asked.
The schedules belong to the students: their own.
Intensifier before the comparative: much longer.

gaps.hint: pronoun: a name: ___ is called the planning fallacy
gaps.explanation: 'It is called…' — the passive formula describing the name.
Contrastive sentence adverb between commas: However.

gaps.hint: conjunction: the best case is imaginable, ___ the traffic
gaps.explanation: Contrast between the two halves: while.

gaps.hint: question word: ask ___ actually happened last time
gaps.explanation: Fused relative object of 'ask': what happened.
